prompt:
On-call chat, #inc-checkout, 02:14 local time.

Priya (SRE): Checkout API p95 latency at ExampleMart jumped from 180 ms to 2.4 s at 01:52. Error rate is 3.1%, mostly HTTP 504 from the edge load balancer. Nothing was deployed tonight. The payments database CPU is at 35%, which is normal. One of the four app nodes, app-03 (10.20.4.13), shows 900 established connections to the database; the other three show about 120 each. Its JVM heap graph is flat.

You are the incident commander. Reply in the channel with: a severity call and why, the first three things to check in order, who to page, and what to say in the first status-page update. Keep it short enough to read on a phone.

Example Freight's edge router edge-rtr-1 lost its eBGP session to our transit provider three times in the last hour. Each time it comes back within two minutes. Relevant output:

edge-rtr-1# show ip bgp summary | include 203.0.113.1
203.0.113.1  4  64500  18231  17990  8812345  0  0 00:01:42  912344
edge-rtr-1# show logging | include BGP
%BGP-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor 203.0.113.1 Down BGP Notification sent
%BGP-3-NOTIFICATION: sent to neighbor 203.0.113.1 4/0 (hold time expired) 0 bytes
%BGP-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor 203.0.113.1 Up

Our AS is 64510. The router takes a full table. CPU spiked to 97% just before each drop. Explain what these lines tell us, list the likely causes in order, and give the read-only commands I should run next on a Cisco IOS XE router. Do not suggest clearing the session yet.

Two Arista switches at the Example University data center will not form an OSPF adjacency over a new routed link. From core-sw-2:

core-sw-2# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID  Instance VRF      Pri State          Dead Time Address     Interface
10.255.0.1   1        default  1   EXSTART/BDR    00:00:36  10.40.1.1   Ethernet49/1

The state has stayed in EXSTART for 20 minutes. The link was cabled yesterday by a contractor. core-sw-1 uses a 9214-byte MTU on its uplinks, and nobody has confirmed the setting on core-sw-2's new port.

Write a short troubleshooting note for a junior engineer. Explain what EXSTART means, why it gets stuck, how to confirm the cause with show commands on both switches, and the lowest-risk fix.

Users at the Pune office of Example Clinics cannot open intranet.example.com since 09:00. Users at head office can. Pune clients get DNS from a local Windows DNS server, 10.12.0.10, which forwards to head office at 10.1.0.10.

From a Pune laptop:
C:\> nslookup intranet.example.com
Server:  pune-dc01.corp.example.com
Address:  10.12.0.10
*** pune-dc01.corp.example.com can't find intranet.example.com: Non-existent domain

From head office:
$ dig +short intranet.example.com @10.1.0.10
10.1.8.25

Yesterday the web team moved intranet.example.com to a new internal zone. Explain the most likely causes, how to prove which one it is with read-only checks, and the fix. Mention any DNS cache we need to clear and on which server.

Guest Wi-Fi users at the Example Resorts lobby report "Connected, no internet". The guest VLAN is 172.20.30.0/24. The DHCP server is a Linux box running ISC Kea. Its log shows many lines like:

2026-09-12 18:04:11.201 WARN ALLOC_ENGINE_V4_ALLOC_FAIL_SUBNET [hwtype=1 3c:22:fb:9a:10:4e], cid=[no info], tid=0x5c1a2b3d: failed to allocate an IPv4 address in the subnet 172.20.30.0/24, subnet-id 30, shared network (none)
2026-09-12 18:04:13.877 WARN ALLOC_ENGINE_V4_ALLOC_FAIL [hwtype=1 a4:83:e7:21:5c:0b], cid=[no info], tid=0x9e04c711: failed to allocate an IPv4 address after 253 attempt(s)

The lease time is 7 days. A conference with about 400 attendees started today.

Explain what is happening. Give me a short-term fix I can apply tonight with the least risk, and a longer-term design change for the guest network. Include what I should check first to make sure the pool is really exhausted.

Warehouse staff at Example Manufacturing say their handheld scanners drop off Wi-Fi when they walk between aisles 12 and 18. The scanners reconnect after 5 to 10 seconds, and the scan app loses its session. The site uses 22 ceiling-mounted access points on 5 GHz, WPA2-Enterprise, SSID WH-SCAN.

Controller log excerpt for one scanner:
14:02:17 Client 00:1b:44:11:3a:b7 deauthenticated from AP-WH-14, reason 8 (leaving BSS)
14:02:18 Client 00:1b:44:11:3a:b7 associating to AP-WH-16
14:02:23 Client 00:1b:44:11:3a:b7 802.1X authentication complete on AP-WH-16

Fast roaming (802.11r) is disabled. The racks in aisles 12 to 18 are metal and 8 m tall.

Write a site-survey-style assessment: likely causes, what data to collect next, and the configuration changes to test first, in order of risk.

Change review request, CHG-4471, for the Example Bank perimeter firewall.

Requested rule, to be added at the top of the outside-in policy:
  source: any
  destination: 10.30.5.20 (new vendor SFTP server, NAT to 198.51.100.40)
  service: tcp/22, tcp/8443
  action: allow
  logging: off
  justification: "Vendor needs to upload files. Urgent, go-live Friday."

The vendor has told us their upload servers use 192.0.2.0/28. Port 8443 is the server's web admin console.

You are the security reviewer on the change board. Write your review as a short memo: approve, reject, or approve with conditions. List each problem with the rule, the corrected rule you would accept, and any logging or monitoring you require before go-live.

In our staging cluster at Example Games, the orders service cannot reach the inventory service since a platform team change this morning.

$ kubectl -n shop exec deploy/orders -- curl -sS -m 3 http://inventory.shop.svc.cluster.local:8080/health
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 3001 milliseconds
$ kubectl -n shop get endpoints inventory
NAME        ENDPOINTS                         AGE
inventory   10.244.2.17:8080,10.244.3.9:8080  41d
$ kubectl -n shop get networkpolicy
NAME                 POD-SELECTOR     AGE
default-deny-all     <none>           3h
allow-frontend       app=frontend     3h

DNS resolves the service name. The CNI is Calico. Explain the most likely cause, how to confirm it without changing anything, and write the NetworkPolicy YAML that allows only orders to reach inventory on port 8080.

Customers of Example Insurance on some Android phones see "certificate not trusted" on portal.example.com. Desktop browsers work. We renewed the certificate two days ago.

$ openssl s_client -connect portal.example.com:443 -servername portal.example.com </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -E 's:|i:'
 0 s:CN = portal.example.com
   i:C = US, O = Example Trust, CN = Example Trust RSA CA 2026

The old certificate's chain showed two entries. The load balancer's certificate profile was updated by uploading only the new leaf certificate file.

Explain why only some clients fail, how to confirm it with one or two commands, and the exact fix on the load balancer. Add a short checklist we can use for the next renewal so this does not happen again.

The site-to-site IPsec tunnel between Example Foods' Chennai plant and our Azure hub came up after a firewall replacement, but no traffic passes. The new firewall is a FortiGate. Its log shows:

ike 0:AZ-HUB:1203: responder: parsed SA_INIT response
ike 0:AZ-HUB:1203: established IKE SA
ike 0:AZ-HUB:1203:AZ-HUB-P2: IPsec SA connect 0 203.0.113.60->198.51.100.20:0
ike 0:AZ-HUB:1203: notify msg received: TS_UNACCEPTABLE

The plant LAN is 10.60.10.0/24. The Azure VNet is 10.100.0.0/16. The old firewall used one phase 2 selector per subnet; the new one was set up with 0.0.0.0/0 on both sides.

Explain what TS_UNACCEPTABLE means here, what to compare on each side, and the change you would make. Say which side should change and why.

A floor switch at the Example Media office logged this overnight, and three desks lost network this morning:

Sep 14 02:11:08 fl3-acc-2 %SPANTREE-2-BLOCK_BPDUGUARD: Received BPDU on port Gi1/0/23 with BPDU Guard enabled. Disabling port.
Sep 14 02:11:08 fl3-acc-2 %PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Gi1/0/23, putting Gi1/0/23 in err-disable state
Sep 14 02:11:09 fl3-acc-2 %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet1/0/23, changed state to down
Sep 14 07:42:51 fl3-acc-2 %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24, changed state to up

A cleaner reported moving a small desk switch last night.

Explain each line in plain English for the service desk. Then say what probably happened, what to check before re-enabling the port, and the commands to recover it safely. Should we turn on err-disable auto-recovery for bpduguard? Give a recommendation.

Prepare a capacity note for Example Air' IT steering meeting about the 1 Gbps MPLS link to the Bengaluru operations center.

Monthly 95th-percentile inbound utilization:
Apr 510 Mbps, May 560, Jun 610, Jul 655, Aug 720, Sep 790.
Peak 5-minute inbound in September: 968 Mbps, three times, all between 09:00 and 10:00.
About 40% of peak traffic is video from the new crew-training platform, which launched in June.

The carrier needs 60 days to upgrade the link to 2 Gbps. A second 1 Gbps internet circuit already exists at the site and is mostly idle.

Write a one-page note: the trend and when we hit trouble, options (upgrade, offload video, QoS, SD-WAN over the internet circuit) with pros and cons, and a recommendation. State your assumptions.

Draft the implementation and backout plan for a change-advisory-board request at Example Logistics.

Change: upgrade firmware on the two core switches (core-a and core-b, a virtual-chassis pair) from version 23.4R2 to 24.2R1 during the Sunday 01:00-05:00 window. The pair carries all 40 access switches, the data center uplinks, and the voice gateways. The vendor's release notes list an ISSU path but warn that ISSU is "not supported when MACsec is enabled". MACsec is enabled on the data center uplinks.

Write the plan as a checklist with: prechecks, the upgrade sequence, success checks after each step, a clear stop condition, the backout procedure, and the communication plan. Say whether you would use ISSU and why.

Write a blameless postmortem from this timeline. The audience is engineering leadership at Example Payments.

Timeline (UTC):
13:02 A certificate-rotation script updates the internal CA bundle on all API gateways.
13:05 Mobile app login failures rise to 22%.
13:09 On-call engineer is paged by the login error-rate alert.
13:21 Team suspects the identity provider and opens a vendor ticket.
13:48 An engineer notices the gateways log "unable to get local issuer certificate" when calling the token service.
13:55 The CA bundle change is rolled back.
14:03 Login failures return to baseline.

The rotation script had been tested only in staging, where the token service uses a different certificate chain.

Include: summary, impact, root cause, contributing factors, what went well, and action items with owners as roles and a priority each.

Draft a runbook for testing failover of the HA firewall pair at Example Credit Union's main branch. The pair is two Palo Alto firewalls in active/passive mode. They connect to two ISPs, and HA links run over two dedicated cables.

The test must happen in the Saturday 22:00-23:00 window. The branch runs ATMs that must not lose their connection to the processor for more than 30 seconds.

The runbook should have: purpose and scope, prerequisites, a pre-test checklist, step-by-step failover and failback with the exact read-only checks to run at each step, success criteria, abort criteria, and a rollback section. Write it for an engineer who has not done this before. Use numbered steps.

Our monitoring at Example Dairy sends about 300 disk-space alerts a week. On-call engineers now ignore them. The current rule is:

  alert: DiskSpaceLow
  expr: node_filesystem_avail_bytes / node_filesystem_size_bytes < 0.20
  for: 5m
  labels: severity=page

Most alerts come from 60 database servers with 4 TB volumes that sit at 15-18% free for weeks. Two real outages last quarter came from log volumes that filled within two hours.

Propose a better alerting design. Include rewritten Prometheus rules (for example, a time-to-full prediction and a ticket-level warning), which alerts should page and which should not, and how to roll the change out without missing a real incident.

After adding a new spoke VPC, instances in it at Example Travel cannot reach our shared-services VPC through the AWS Transit Gateway.

New spoke VPC: 10.70.0.0/16, attached to the TGW, association and propagation to the "spokes" route table.
Shared services VPC: 10.10.0.0/16, attached, associated with the "shared" route table.

$ aws ec2 search-transit-gateway-routes --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-shared --filters Name=type,Values=propagated
Routes: 10.20.0.0/16, 10.30.0.0/16 (no 10.70.0.0/16)

The spoke VPC's subnet route table has 10.10.0.0/16 pointing to the TGW. Security groups allow ICMP and TCP 443 from 10.70.0.0/16.

Explain what is missing, the order of the checks you would do, and the exact change needed. Mention anything else in the return path that could still block traffic.

Design an application-aware routing policy for Example Assurance's SD-WAN. Each of the 35 branches has an MPLS circuit and a broadband internet circuit. Branch staff use Microsoft Teams, a claims web app hosted in our data center, and a SaaS CRM.

Last month the MPLS provider had two brownouts. Loss reached 4% and jitter 45 ms for about 20 minutes each time, but the circuit never went down. Calls on Teams were unusable, and the SD-WAN did not move them.

Write the policy: SLA classes with loss, latency, and jitter thresholds for each application, preferred and fallback paths, and how to detect a brownout rather than only a hard failure. Explain the tradeoffs of your thresholds, and how to test the policy at one branch before rollout.

We are rolling out 802.1X on access ports at Example Health. Laptops authenticate fine, but the 60 network printers on floor 2 get no access.

RADIUS log for one printer:
Authentication failed: 5400 Authentication failed
  Endpoint MAC: 00:80:77:4c:1a:02
  Authentication method: dot1x
  Failure reason: 12321 PEAP failed SSL/TLS handshake because the client rejected the ISE local-certificate

Port config on the switch:
  authentication port-control auto
  dot1x pae authenticator
  authentication order dot1x
  authentication priority dot1x

The printers do not support 802.1X well. Explain why they fail, and propose a secure way to onboard them (for example MAB with profiling). Include the switch port configuration changes and the risks of each option.

VMs on one datastore at Example Labs have been slow since Tuesday. Users complain about the file server and a build server. From esxtop on one host, disk device view:

DEVICE                               DAVG/cmd  KAVG/cmd  GAVG/cmd  QUED
naa.600a098038303053453f4b2d6f4c7a41    38.2      0.1      38.3      0
naa.600a098038303053453f4b2d6f4c7a42     2.1      0.0       2.1      0

The first device backs datastore DS-PROD-03. The array team says "no alerts on our side". A nightly backup job was moved to 10:00 on Tuesday to finish earlier.

Explain what DAVG, KAVG, and GAVG tell us here and where the latency is. List what to ask the array team for, what to check on the SAN fabric, and a short-term mitigation. Write it so I can paste it into a ticket to the storage team.

Our weekly report at Example Hotels shows the file-server backup job "FS01-nightly" as "Success with warnings" for the last 12 nights. The warning is:

Warning: 1,843 files skipped (in use or access denied). Job completed.

Nobody has tested a restore of FS01 since March. FS01 holds finance and HR shares. The auditors visit in five weeks and will ask for proof that backups can be restored.

Write a plan for the next five weeks: how to find out what is being skipped and why, how to fix it, and a restore test we can show the auditors. Include what evidence to keep from the test. Also say which skipped-file warnings are acceptable and which are not.

Plan this month's Windows Server patching at Example City Council. There are 140 servers:

- 12 domain controllers across 4 sites
- 6 SQL Server clusters (2 nodes each)
- 40 application servers, some owned by vendors who must approve reboots
- 70 file, print, and utility servers

This month's release includes a critical remote code execution fix that is being exploited in the wild, and the security team wants it everywhere within 7 days. Last month a patch broke a line-of-business app on 3 servers and had to be rolled back.

Write a phased rollout plan: rings, order, timing, testing, how to handle the clusters and domain controllers, vendor approvals, rollback, and how we will report progress to the security team.

Our HAProxy load balancer at Example Fashion keeps marking healthy backends as DOWN for a few seconds, then UP again. Users see intermittent 503 errors.

backend web_pool
  option httpchk GET /health
  http-check expect status 200
  timeout check 1s
  default-server inter 2s fall 2 rise 2
  server web1 10.8.1.11:8080 check
  server web2 10.8.1.12:8080 check

HAProxy log:
Server web_pool/web1 is DOWN, reason: Layer7 timeout, check duration: 1001ms.
Server web_pool/web1 is UP, reason: Layer7 check passed, code: 200, check duration: 212ms.

The /health endpoint on the app queries the database. Database load peaks every 15 minutes during a batch job. Explain the cause, what to change in the check, and whether /health should query the database at all.

Since last night, some users at Example Savings' Dublin office cannot log on. The error is "The time difference between the client and server is too great". Domain controller DC-DUB-01 shows:

C:\> w32tm /query /status
Leap Indicator: 0(no warning)
Stratum: 1 (primary reference - syncd by radio clock)
Source: Local CMOS Clock
Last Successful Sync Time: 14/09/2026 23:58:10

C:\> w32tm /monitor /computers:DC-HQ-01
DC-HQ-01.corp.example.com[10.1.0.11:123]:
    ICMP: 1ms delay
    NTP: -312.4480000s offset from DC-DUB-01.corp.example.com

DC-DUB-01 is a VM that was migrated to a new hypervisor host yesterday. Explain what is wrong, the safe order of fixes, and the correct time hierarchy for domain controllers. Warn me about anything that could make it worse.

Service desk ticket at Example Engineering: "Printer PRN-2F-07 (192.168.40.57) keeps going offline for a few minutes at a time."

From the core switch:
core# show ip arp 192.168.40.57
Internet  192.168.40.57   0   0080.774c.1a07  ARPA  Vlan40
(two minutes later)
Internet  192.168.40.57   0   5c26.0a91.33fe  ARPA  Vlan40
core# show mac address-table address 5c26.0a91.33fe
  40    5c26.0a91.33fe    DYNAMIC     Gi2/0/14

The printer has a static IP. The DHCP scope for VLAN 40 is 192.168.40.20-192.168.40.200.

Explain what is happening, how to find the other device and its owner, and a fix that stops it from happening again. Include what to change in DHCP and in the IP address records.
